name: Product Requirements Discovery
objective: Turn a rough idea or a discovered opportunity into a reviewable, implementation-ready specification by interviewing the idea owner about the problem, users, functionality, workflows, business rules, constraints, integrations, security, data, technical preferences and edge cases.

contextBlock.question: Where will this run? Existing infrastructure, a cloud account, a managed platform, or nothing yet?
contextBlock.questionNontechnical: Do you already have somewhere this would run, like a company server or a cloud account, or is that still open?
contextBlock.why: Hosting changes architecture, cost, and compliance defaults.

options.label: Cloud account
options.detail: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Hetzner, or similar

contextBlock.question: Which existing systems must this work with?
contextBlock.questionNontechnical: Which tools or systems does this need to connect to, if any?
contextBlock.why: Integrations shape data requirements and effort.

contextBlock.question: Who will build it?
contextBlock.why: Decides how the specification and plan are phrased.

contextBlock.question: What does the team know best?
contextBlock.questionNontechnical: If someone technical is involved, what do they usually work with?
contextBlock.why: A stack the team knows beats a marginally better stack.

contextBlock.question: When does version one need to exist?
How many users at launch, roughly?
Any compliance needs? Personal data, health, finance, public sector?
contextBlock.why: Changes data, hosting, and security requirements.

coverageAreas.name: Product overview and problem
coverageAreas.description: What problem, for whom, why now.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Problem statement with who has it and what happens if unsolved.

coverageAreas.name: Target users and roles
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each role has a goal and a first action.

coverageAreas.name: User stories
coverageAreas.description: What each role does with the product.

coverageAreas.name: Functional requirements
coverageAreas.description: Capabilities, each tagged mvp or future.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Every requirement has an id, a tag and at least one acceptance criterion.

coverageAreas.name: Business rules
coverageAreas.description: Rules and edge cases that govern behavior.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Rules exist for every decision point in the flows.

coverageAreas.name: Technical requirements
coverageAreas.description: Backend, frontend, database, hosting, auth, architecture. One decision per question, each with a default.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each decision is made or its default accepted.
coverageAreas.instructions: Never bundle stack decisions. Never default a technology before the team_skills context answer is known.

coverageAreas.name: Technical recommendations
coverageAreas.description: Derived technical choices explained in plain language.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: The user has confirmed or asked about each recommendation.
coverageAreas.instructions: Present each recommendation with a one-line reason; ask only for confirmation or questions.

coverageAreas.name: Data requirements
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Entities and relationships are listed with retention.

coverageAreas.name: Integrations
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each integration has direction, data and auth.

coverageAreas.name: Security and privacy
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Roles, data classes and compliance needs are known.

coverageAreas.name: Non-functional requirements
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Targets are numbers or explicitly deferred.

coverageAreas.name: Administrative surface
coverageAreas.description: What operators and admins need to configure and see. Enumerate it explicitly.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: The admin surface is listed and each item is mvp or future.

coverageAreas.name: MVP scope
coverageAreas.description: The smallest version that solves the core problem.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Owner has confirmed the mvp set and challenged items were resolved.

coverageAreas.name: Future scope
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Deferred items are listed with the reason.

coverageAreas.name: Implementation phases
coverageAreas.description: Ordered, independently testable phases for a developer or coding agent.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each phase has tasks, dependencies and acceptance.

aiInstructions: Ask one decision per question when the build impact is high; never bundle. Every question states why it matters and offers a default the user can accept in one word. On the nontechnical path, ask about behavior in plain language and present technical choices as recommendations with a one-line reason. On the technical path, ask architecture, API and data questions and record alternatives considered. Enumerate administrative surfaces explicitly and ask what is missing. Challenge MVP items that are not needed to solve the core problem. Flag conflicts between a choice and the context block answers.
closingQuestion: Is there anything about this product we have not covered that a developer would need to know?
